thread:
Maya: quick pulse check — ran a microthreshold sweep on the new 11B candidate (nyx-lite) with int6 and int4 drops. need a short scorecard we can hand to GTN/product by EOD. what's the delta on unit econ and quality signals?

Raj: short answer: int6 looks promising, int4 has some regression on factuality for longform answers. numbers below.

Tess: can you paste the slice breakdown? product cares about longform + code tasks specifically.

Raj: sure — here's the cleaned summary from last night's run (n=2k samples mixed longform/qa/code):

```
variant  | tokens/sent | p95 latency | cost/unit ($) | helpfulness Δ | factuality Δ
baseline (13B fp16) | 3800        | 420ms       | 0.012         | 0.0           | 0.0
nyx-lite int6        | 3700        | 450ms       | 0.0066        | -0.03         | -0.02
nyx-lite int4        | 3600        | 480ms       | 0.0048        | -0.07         | -0.06
```

Raj: helpfulness/factuality are normalized deltas vs baseline (higher is better).

Maya: ok so int6 = ~45% cost reduction with <3% helpfulness drop and ~2% factuality drop — that's probably acceptable for most product slices. int4 saves ~60% but starts bleeding quality.

Ciara: what's the user-visible latency impact? p95 went from 420ms -> 450/480ms. Product will flag higher tail for chat heavy flows. Any way to regain tail?

Oliver: we saw that increasing micro-batching window from 10ms -> 20ms recovers ~30ms on p95 at ~2% throughput loss. also KV cache warmstart helps for multi-turn.

Tess: flags for GTN: recommend int6 by default for read-mostly flows, int4 only for low-risk emb/summary jobs or behind strict fallback. Need a one-paragraph exec rec + bullets.

Maya: draft rec — can someone sanity-check?

Ciara: quick edit suggestions inline: keep it punchy.

Maya: pasted draft — please react +1 or suggest changes:

"Exec rec: Deploy nyx-lite int6 as our preferred cost-quality tradeoff for consumer chat pilot. It reduces per-unit cost by ~45% vs 13B fp16 with minimal quality degradation (helpfulness -3%, factuality -2%). Hold int4 for non-critical background generation (summaries, embeddings) and performance experiments; require a small canary (1%) + automated eval on our longform slice before broader rollout."

Raj: nit: change '1%' canary to '0.5% for initial shadow traffic then 1% live' — gives ops time to catch tail regressions.

ops-bot: scheduled canary rollout window 2026-04-02T15:00Z -> 2026-04-03T03:00Z (created by Maya).

Tess: also add these operational controls to the rec:
- automatic rollback trigger if factuality Δ <= -5% on the longform slice over 12h
- p95 latency degradation > +100ms over baseline -> throttle to int6 or fallback to 13B fp16
- daily sample drift check (1000 samples) for hallucination rate

Maya: final ask for GTN: short 3-metric scorecard (cost reduction, helpfulness Δ, factuality Δ) + one-line ops conditions. I'll format and send. add any final bullets now.

Oliver: add note — recommend enabling kv-warmstart for chat to reduce tail and enable 20ms batching for stable flows. include expected trade (2% throughput loss).

Ciara: +1. Also flag product: int6 will change token billing patterns; show them per-100k token cost impact.

Raj: sample per-100k token cost calc: baseline = $1.2, nyx-lite int6 = $0.66, nyx-lite int4 = $0.48.

Maya: perfect. I'll stitch this into a compact thread message for GTN and attach the raw sweep csv to the doc. Thanks all :thumbsup:
